# Question: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible rival is:

> Apply the correct row/column span logic only to colors that occur exactly
> twice in the **entire grid**. Ignore any color whose global multiplicity is
> not two.

This fits every canonical demonstration because each nonzero color occurs
exactly twice globally in all five canonical inputs. It also fit all 600 sampled
v3.0.0 generations in the initial review census.

An exact disagreement input is:

```text
00000000
02000200
00000040
00000000
00000000
00000042
00000000
```

Color 2 occurs three times globally: at `(1,1)`, `(1,5)`, and `(5,7)` using
zero-based coordinates. On row 1, however, it occurs exactly twice and its
strict interior is zero. Color 4 forms an ordinary clear vertical pair.

The intended output is:

```text
00000000
02222200
00000040
00000040
00000040
00000042
00000000
```

The global-exactly-two rival instead produces:

```text
00000000
02000200
00000040
00000040
00000040
00000042
00000000
```

It fills color 4 but incorrectly suppresses the horizontal color-2 span.

I checked the intended output in two independent paths: the generator’s
input-pure Python mirror and the bundled protected Racket runtime executing the
canonical `program_solution` with rule hash `3c80c97f70dc`. They agreed exactly.
The retained Racket probe also compared 150 generated repeated-color cases and
found zero mirror mismatches.

The revised generator does emit such cases. Schedule profile 3 gives one active
color an off-axis third occurrence, so every four consecutive generated
examples contain a counterexample to this rival. The retained census checked
4,800 examples across easy, medium, and hard bands and eight rolling window
starts: 1,200 repeated-color cases, 1,200 rival disagreements, and zero
four-example windows without a refutation.
